events.reason: sudden shortness of breath and left chest pain

conditions.label: Traumatic diaphragmatic hernia
conditions.note: left-sided, delayed presentation of 2019 blunt trauma

reports.text: Single upright AP view of the chest. The left hemidiaphragm is elevated, and gas-filled loops of bowel project over the left lower and mid thorax. The mediastinum is shifted toward the right. The right lung is clear. No pneumothorax.
reports.conclusion: Elevated left hemidiaphragm with bowel loops in the left hemithorax and rightward mediastinal shift, consistent with diaphragmatic hernia.

reports.text: CT chest with IV contrast, including the upper abdomen. There is a defect in the left hemidiaphragm through which loops of bowel herniate into the left thorax, with rightward mediastinal shift. Herniated bowel enhances normally; no free air or pneumatosis. No pleural effusion. No pneumothorax. Heart size normal.
reports.conclusion: Left diaphragmatic defect with herniated bowel into the left chest and mediastinal shift. Bowel enhancement preserved.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain
Take 2 tablets by mouth every 8 hours as needed for pain

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Hospital emergency department
Date of service: 01/17/2025

CC: abrupt shortness of breath and pain on the left side of the chest.

HPI: 36M, photographer, with a past collision that broke several ribs and bruised his lung. This afternoon he became suddenly short of breath with left chest pain. No fever or cough.

PMH (per prior records): hepatitis A susceptibility, CSF rhinorrhea, healed rib fractures, resolved pulmonary contusion, mild TBI. PSH: none. Meds: multivitamin. Allergies: NKDA. FHx: father HTN; no autoimmune or bleeding disorders. SHx: never smoker, social alcohol 2-3/week.

Vitals on arrival: BP 130/85, HR 105, RR 22, SpO2 92% on room air.
Exam: breath sounds diminished over the left chest, tympanic to percussion on that side. Right chest clear. Abdomen soft.

Labs: CBC and chemistries within normal limits.
Upright CXR: elevated left hemidiaphragm, bowel loops in the left chest, mediastinum pushed to the right.
CT chest: left diaphragmatic defect with herniated bowel, enhancement preserved.

Assessment: traumatic diaphragmatic hernia, presenting late after prior blunt trauma.

Plan: NG decompression, supplemental oxygen, general surgery consulted, admitted to surgery for repair.

Allergies: NKDA. Copy to primary care.

documents.title: Operative Report
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Hospital general surgery
Date of operation: 01/18/2025

Preoperative diagnosis: left traumatic diaphragmatic hernia.
Postoperative diagnosis: same.
Procedure: laparoscopic reduction of hernia contents and primary repair of left diaphragm.
Anesthesia: general endotracheal.

Findings: defect in the left hemidiaphragm with herniated bowel loops into the left chest. Contents reduced without difficulty; bowel pink, peristalsing and viable throughout, no resection needed. Defect closed primarily with interrupted nonabsorbable sutures. Left chest re-expanded under positive pressure; no chest tube needed.

EBL minimal. No complications. To recovery in stable condition.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Hospital general surgery
Admitted 01/17/2025, discharged 01/21/2025.

Diagnosis: traumatic left diaphragmatic hernia, delayed presentation.
Procedure: laparoscopic reduction and primary repair 01/18/2025.

Course: presented through the ED with acute dyspnea and left chest pain; imaging showed bowel in the left chest. Repaired the next morning. Oxygen weaned off on postoperative day 1, diet advanced, ambulating, pain controlled on oral medication. Discharged home on hospital day 5.

Discharge medications: oxycodone 5 mg every 6 hours as needed (#12), acetaminophen 1000 mg every 8 hours as needed, home multivitamin.
Instructions: no lifting over 10 lb for six weeks; may shower; surgical clinic follow-up in about three weeks.

Allergies: NKDA. Copy to primary care physician.

documents.title: Hospital records filed
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Operative report and discharge summary for January admission received today after second request. Scanned and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Home from hospital
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called. Was admitted Fri 1/17 with a diaphragm hernia, had laparoscopic surgery Sat, discharged yesterday. Pain manageable, using the oxycodone mostly at night plus Tylenol. Breathing comfortably, no fever, eating. Pharmacy fill history shows oxycodone 5 mg #12 filled 1/21. No hospital paperwork here yet. Scheduled post-hospital visit 1/29. Advised ER for fever, worsening shortness of breath or vomiting.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-discharge visit. Admitted 1/17 to 1/21 for a left diaphragmatic hernia, felt to be from the 2019 crash, missed at the time. Laparoscopic repair 1/18 per patient and ED record (received 1/24); op note and discharge summary not yet received.

Now: soreness at the port sites, improving. Stopped the oxycodone 2 days ago, using acetaminophen occasionally. No shortness of breath, cough, fever, nausea or vomiting. Bowels moving normally. Walking a few miles a day.

Meds: multivitamin, acetaminophen as needed. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted, SpO2 normal on room air. Comfortable. Breath sounds equal bilaterally, no tympany. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, appropriately tender near port sites, incisions clean and dry, no erythema or drainage.

A/P: s/p laparoscopic repair of traumatic diaphragmatic hernia, recovering as expected.
- Lifting limit 10 lb until early March per surgery.
- Surgical follow-up already scheduled.
- Records request sent to hospital for op note and discharge summary.
- Call for fever, worsening pain, shortness of breath.

documents.title: Surgeon visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw the surgeon yesterday. All healed, he's happy. Still no lifting heavy camera stuff until early March and then I can go back to normal. FYI in case you don't get a letter.

documents.title: RE: Surgeon visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks, Nathan, good to hear. Noted in your chart.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Nathan, we missed you for your physical yesterday morning. Would you like to rebook?

documents.title: RE: Missed appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: So sorry, I was out on a shoot before dawn and completely lost track. Any morning the week of July 7 works.

documents.title: RE: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: You're booked Thursday 7/10 at 8:00. Come fasting if you can.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly exam, rescheduled from 6/26. Fully back to work and hiking with full packs since March. No chest pain, shortness of breath, reflux or bowel trouble since the January surgery. No nasal drainage. No headaches.

Meds: multivitamin. NKDA.
Social: never smoker; a few drinks a week. Same partner, same work.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight back to his usual. Well. Nares clear. Lungs clear with equal breath sounds both bases. Heart RRR. Abdomen soft, nontender, port scars well healed. No hernia at port sites. Neuro nonfocal.

PHQ-2 0.

A/P:
1. Annual preventive: CBC, CMP, lipids today.
2. Traumatic diaphragmatic hernia, repaired 1/2025: healed, no symptoms. Resolving on problem list.
3. Hep A series complete 2024. Tdap good to 2029. Flu and COVID this fall.
RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Nathan, your labs from yesterday are normal. No changes needed. See you next summer, or sooner if anything comes up.

documents.title: Pharmacy immunization report
documents.author: pharmacy
documents.body: Community pharmacy immunization notification. Influenza vaccine, trivalent, 0.5 mL IM, left deltoid, administered 10/18/2025. No adverse reaction observed. Filed to immunization history.

documents.title: Call from hospital ICU
documents.author: RN
documents.body: ICU nurse at an outside hospital called. Patient admitted to their ICU overnight; they are asking for his immunization history, specifically any rabies vaccine. Reviewed our record: no rabies vaccine ever documented. Hep A x2 (12/2023, 8/2024), Tdap 8/2019, flu and COVID per record. Immunization record faxed to the ICU. PCP notified.

documents.title: PCP note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Aware. Asked ICU to send admission records.

documents.title: ICU Admission Note
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
Outside hospital medical ICU
Date of admission: 11/23/2025

CC: fever, headache and confusion for two days; tingling around an old scratch on the left forearm.

HPI: 37M. History of traumatic injuries including rib fractures, pulmonary contusion, mild TBI and a diaphragmatic hernia. Two days of fever and headache, now confused. He describes pins-and-needles around a healed wound on the left forearm. He remembers a bat scratching him there about two months ago while camping; he did not seek care at the time.

PMH (outside list): hepatitis A susceptibility, CSF rhinorrhea, traumatic diaphragmatic hernia, healed rib fractures, resolved pulmonary contusion, mild TBI. PSH: none listed. Home meds: multivitamin daily. Allergies: NKDA. FHx: father with treated hypertension; no autoimmune or bleeding disorders. SHx: never smoker, social alcohol, wildlife photographer.

Vitals: T 38.9 C, HR 110, BP 145/90.
Exam: agitated. Excess salivation; difficulty swallowing when offered water. Hyperreflexic. Encephalopathic. Healed scratch on left forearm; no other wounds or signs of infection.

Labs: WBC 11.0, Hgb 14.2, Plt 250. Na 135, K 4.0, BUN 14, Cr 1.0, glucose 98. CSF: lymphocytic pleocytosis, glucose and protein normal.

Assessment: clinical rabies, symptomatic phase, after bat exposure.

Plan: ICU admission, precautions and supportive care. Rabies diagnostics (saliva, serum, CSF, nuchal skin biopsy) sent to the state public health laboratory, results pending.

Allergies: NKDA. Copy to primary care physician.

documents.title: ICU records filed
documents.author: MA
documents.body: ICU admission note from 11/23 received by fax. Scanned to chart, routed to PCP.
